title: Azure AI Fundamentals
subtitle: Jeopardy Review

gradeLabels.f: F-RANK -- Back to the Training Data

jeopardyFormatExample.clueText: This generative-AI failure mode is when a model produces plausible-sounding but factually FALSE information

categoryLegend: AI Workloads & Responsible AI: computer vision, NLP, generative AI, the 6 principles.  Machine Learning Fundamentals: supervised, unsupervised, regression, classification, clustering.  Model Evaluation & Azure ML: accuracy, precision, recall, AutoML, Designer.  Computer Vision: image classification, object detection, OCR, Azure AI Vision.  NLP & Speech: sentiment, key phrases, NER, CLU, Azure AI Language, Speech.  Generative AI & Azure OpenAI: LLMs, tokens, prompting, grounding, Azure OpenAI Service.

clues.clue: This AI workload category focuses on training models with labeled data to make predictions about new, unseen inputs.
clues.explain: Machine learning is one of the core AI workload categories in which algorithms learn patterns from data to make predictions or decisions. It is the foundation of most modern AI applications.

clues.clue: This Microsoft Responsible AI principle requires that AI systems serve ALL users equitably, including those with disabilities, by prioritizing accessibility.
clues.explain: Inclusiveness means AI systems should benefit all people regardless of ability, age, gender, or background. It specifically calls out accessibility as a key design requirement so that no group is left behind.

clues.clue: This AI workload category uses techniques such as full-text search and information extraction to surface insights from large repositories of unstructured content like documents and PDFs.
clues.response: What is knowledge mining (or document intelligence)?
clues.explain: Knowledge mining and document intelligence focus on extracting structured insights from unstructured sources such as scanned documents, PDFs, and form data. Azure AI Document Intelligence is the primary service for this workload.

clues.clue: Of the six Microsoft Responsible AI principles, this one mandates that humans remain responsible for AI-based decisions and that audit trails exist to trace how outcomes were reached.
clues.explain: Accountability holds that people and organizations must be answerable for the behavior of AI systems they design and deploy. It requires governance processes and audit mechanisms so human oversight is preserved.

clues.clue: This AI workload category detects unusual patterns in data — such as sudden spikes in network traffic or unexpected dips in manufacturing output — that deviate significantly from the norm.
clues.explain: Anomaly detection identifies data points that fall outside expected patterns, making it useful for fraud detection, predictive maintenance, and security monitoring. It is one of the distinct AI workload categories on the AI-900 exam.

clues.clue: In supervised learning, this term refers to the input variables — the columns of data the model uses to make its prediction.
clues.explain: Features (often called x-variables or predictors) are the measurable properties used as inputs to a machine learning model. For example, square footage and number of bedrooms are features when predicting house prices.

clues.clue: This supervised learning task predicts a continuous numeric output, such as the expected sale price of a home given its size and location.
clues.explain: Regression models learn to predict a number on a continuous scale rather than a discrete category. Classic examples include predicting house prices, temperatures, or sales revenue.

clues.clue: Unlike supervised learning, this machine learning approach works with data that has NO labels, grouping similar items together based purely on the patterns it finds in the input.
clues.explain: Unsupervised learning discovers hidden structure in unlabeled data. Because there are no correct answers provided during training, the algorithm must find patterns on its own, most commonly through clustering.

clues.clue: In this type of machine learning, an agent repeatedly interacts with an environment, taking actions and receiving rewards or penalties until it learns a policy that maximizes cumulative reward.
clues.explain: Reinforcement learning trains an agent through trial and error by rewarding desired behaviors and penalizing undesired ones. It has been used to master complex games and optimize robotic control systems.

clues.clue: This machine learning approach uses architectures composed of many interconnected layers of artificial neurons to automatically learn hierarchical representations directly from raw data such as images or audio.
clues.explain: Deep learning uses multi-layer neural networks where each layer learns increasingly abstract representations. It powers breakthroughs in computer vision, speech recognition, and natural language processing by learning features automatically rather than requiring manual feature engineering.

clues.clue: After training a model on the training set, you evaluate its real-world performance on this separate portion of the data, which the model has never seen during training.
clues.explain: Evaluating on the test set gives an unbiased estimate of how the model will perform on new data. Using test data during training would cause data leakage and produce falsely optimistic performance metrics.

clues.clue: This regression evaluation metric represents the proportion of variance in the target variable that the model explains, ranging from 0 (no explanatory power) to 1 (perfect fit).
clues.explain: R² tells you how much of the variability in the outcome is accounted for by the model's predictions. An R² of 0.85 means the model explains 85% of the variance in the target variable.

clues.clue: This classification metric answers the question: 'Of all the items the model predicted as positive, what fraction were actually positive?' Its formula is TP divided by the sum of TP and FP.
clues.explain: Precision measures how trustworthy the model's positive predictions are by calculating TP/(TP+FP). High precision means few false alarms; it is especially important when the cost of a false positive is high.

clues.clue: This Azure Machine Learning feature lets you provide your dataset and designate a label column, and the service then automatically tries multiple algorithms and hyperparameter combinations, returning a ranked leaderboard of trained models.
clues.explain: Azure AutoML automates the time-consuming steps of featurization, algorithm selection, and hyperparameter tuning. It returns a ranked list of candidate models so data scientists can quickly identify the best performer without writing training code.

clues.clue: This classification evaluation metric answers the question: 'Of all the items that were ACTUALLY positive, what fraction did the model correctly identify?' Its formula is TP divided by the sum of TP and FN.
clues.explain: Recall, also called sensitivity or true positive rate, is calculated as TP/(TP+FN). It is critical in domains like medical diagnosis where missing a true positive (a false negative) carries serious consequences.

clues.clue: This computer vision task assigns a single label to an entire image — for example, classifying a photo as 'cat' or 'dog' — without locating any specific objects within it.
clues.explain: Image classification predicts what an image depicts as a whole by assigning one label per image. It answers the question 'What is this a picture of?' rather than 'Where are the objects in this picture?'

clues.clue: This Azure AI service is the pre-built offering for analyzing images, generating captions, detecting objects, and extracting printed or handwritten text via its Read API.
clues.explain: Azure AI Vision (formerly Azure Cognitive Services Computer Vision) provides ready-to-use endpoints for image analysis, OCR, spatial analysis, and the Read API for high-accuracy text extraction. It requires no model training for common tasks.

clues.clue: Unlike image classification, this computer vision task draws a precise rectangular bounding box around each individual object in an image AND predicts a label for every box found.
clues.explain: Object detection locates each instance of objects in an image and classifies them individually, returning both coordinates for each bounding box and the corresponding class label. It answers both 'what' and 'where' for every detected item.

clues.clue: This Azure AI service allows you to train your OWN image classifier or object detector by uploading your labeled images through a portal or SDK, without needing to write model training code.
clues.response: What is Azure AI Custom Vision?
clues.explain: Azure AI Custom Vision lets developers build specialized image classifiers and object detectors by uploading and tagging their own training images. The service handles training, evaluation, and deployment of the resulting model.

clues.clue: This advanced computer vision task goes beyond bounding boxes by classifying EVERY INDIVIDUAL PIXEL in an image as belonging to a particular class, such as road, sky, pedestrian, or building.
clues.explain: Semantic segmentation assigns a class label to each pixel, producing a detailed map of what category every part of the image belongs to. It is more granular than object detection and is commonly used in autonomous vehicle perception and medical imaging.

clues.clue: This NLP task analyzes a piece of text — such as a customer review — and returns a judgment of whether the expressed opinion is positive, negative, neutral, or mixed.
clues.explain: Sentiment analysis classifies the emotional tone of text using pre-trained language models. Azure AI Language provides a sentiment analysis endpoint that returns a label and confidence score for positive, negative, neutral, or mixed sentiment.

clues.clue: This Azure AI service provides both Speech-to-Text transcription and Text-to-Speech synthesis, including lifelike neural voices, for building voice-enabled applications.
clues.explain: Azure AI Speech bundles Speech-to-Text (real-time and batch transcription), Text-to-Speech (including custom neural voices), Speaker Recognition, and Speech Translation into a single unified service. It is the correct AI-900 service name for voice capabilities.

clues.clue: This NLP task scans text and identifies and categorizes real-world entities such as people, organizations, locations, dates, and quantities — for example, recognizing 'Microsoft' as an organization.
clues.explain: NER detects mentions of real-world entities in text and classifies them into predefined categories such as Person, Organization, Location, and Date. Azure AI Language includes NER as one of its built-in text analysis features.

clues.clue: In Conversational Language Understanding (CLU), this element represents the ACTION the user wants to take — for example, 'book_flight' when a user says 'I want to fly to Miami on Friday.'
clues.explain: An intent captures the goal or purpose behind a user's utterance. CLU models are trained to classify each utterance into one of several defined intents, such as book_flight, cancel_reservation, or check_status.

clues.clue: In a CLU model, after the intent 'book_flight' is recognized, the model also extracts these specific details from the utterance — such as the destination city 'Miami' and the date 'Friday' — to complete the action.
clues.explain: Entities are the specific data values extracted from an utterance that are needed to fulfill the recognized intent. In CLU, entities complement intents by providing the parameters the application needs to carry out the user's request.

clues.clue: This problem occurs when a large language model produces output that sounds plausible and confident but is factually incorrect — essentially making something up that was never in its training data.
clues.explain: Hallucination is a well-known limitation of LLMs in which the model generates false information presented as fact. It happens because LLMs predict likely next tokens rather than verifying facts, so they can produce convincing-sounding errors.

clues.clue: This Azure service hosts OpenAI models — including GPT-4 for chat, DALL-E for image generation, and Whisper for speech-to-text — with enterprise security, private networking, and built-in content filtering.
clues.explain: Azure OpenAI Service gives organizations access to OpenAI's foundation models within the Azure cloud, with features like virtual network integration, managed identity, content safety filters, and Azure's compliance certifications. It is distinct from OpenAI's public API.

clues.clue: This prompt engineering technique reduces hallucination by providing the language model with relevant source documents at inference time, grounding its response in retrieved evidence rather than relying solely on training data.
clues.explain: RAG combines a retrieval step — fetching relevant documents from a knowledge base — with the generation step of an LLM, so the model can cite and reason over provided source material. This significantly reduces hallucination for factual queries.

clues.clue: This prompt engineering technique provides a language model with several worked examples of the desired input-output pattern within the prompt itself before asking it to handle a new, unseen input.
clues.explain: Few-shot prompting places two to five labeled examples directly in the prompt so the model learns the expected format or reasoning style from context rather than from fine-tuning. It contrasts with zero-shot prompting, which provides no examples at all.

clues.clue: In a large language model, this controls the randomness of token selection during generation: setting it to 0 makes the model deterministic and always pick the highest-probability token, while higher values produce more varied and creative output.
clues.explain: Temperature scales the probability distribution over possible next tokens before sampling. A temperature of 0 collapses the distribution to always choose the top token (greedy decoding), while values above 1 flatten the distribution and increase creative variability.
